items.title: Declare the assertion envelope schema with unique matcher ids and a kind enum limited to literal-line and class with no pattern language
items.context: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/envelope.ts declares the section 1.1 envelope: matcher ids unique within the envelope; kind restricted to the closed set {literal-line, class}; NO pattern/regex dialect exists anywhere in the type or the validator (section 1.11 rule 1 pins literal-line as a whole-line trimmed string comparison, nothing compiled).

happy.desc: Envelope with two matchers having unique ids and kinds literal-line + class passes schema validation with no rejections; WHY: validates the schema declaration accepts legal envelopes

verification.selector: CHK-001: unique ids across kinds literal-line + class

happy.desc: Envelope with 1..maxMatchers matchers all with unique ids accepted; WHY: array count within policy bounds

verification.selector: CHK-015: exactly policy.maxMatchers=8 matchers (inclusive upper count bound)

edge.desc: Envelope with duplicate matcher id rejected R1-3; WHY: uniqueness constraint is enforceable
Envelope with kind anchored-regex rejected R1-3; WHY: pattern language removed in rev 6, closed enum
Envelope with 0 matchers rejected R1-3; WHY: at least one matcher required
Envelope with maxMatchers+1 matchers rejected R1-3; WHY: policy upper bound enforced

adversarial.desc: Envelope with kind Literal-Line (case variation) rejected R1-3; WHY: enum is case-sensitive, no normalization
Envelope with kind regex rejected R1-3; WHY: no pattern language exists even under alias names
Class matcher with value naming no registry entry rejected R1-3; WHY: class value must be exact case-sensitive registry name

verification.selector: CHK-016: class value "no-such-class" names no registry entry

verificationEvidence.note: red-w2d-rejection-matrix accept() row "CHK-001: unique ids across kinds literal-line + class" validates a two-matcher envelope (id L1 kind literal-line, id C1 kind class value stderr-nonempty) and asserts result.ok === true with a /^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$/ assertionDigest, i.e. zero rejections for a legal envelope spanning both kinds with distinct ids.

items.title: Validate supplementaryArtifact targetArtifactRef path syntax rejecting absolute, empty, dot, dot-dot and backslash segments
items.context: Section 1.1: targetArtifactRef is slash-normalized and validated SYNTACTICALLY (realpath cannot classify a path that does not yet exist, which is the RED case). Absolute paths and empty/dot/dot-dot/backslash segments reject.

happy.desc: targetArtifactRef packages/main/dist/tasks/foo.js accepted; WHY: valid repo-relative slash-separated path with no traversal

edge.desc: targetArtifactRef /absolute/path rejected R1-3; WHY: absolute paths rejected at schema time
targetArtifactRef foo//bar rejected R1-3; WHY: empty segment between consecutive slashes
targetArtifactRef foo/./bar rejected R1-3; WHY: dot segment is traversal
targetArtifactRef foo/../bar rejected R1-3; WHY: dot-dot segment is parent traversal
targetArtifactRef with backslash character rejected R1-3; WHY: backslash rejected for slash-normalization
targetArtifactRef empty string rejected R1-3; WHY: empty path is invalid

adversarial.desc: targetArtifactRef . (bare dot as entire path) rejected R1-3; WHY: single dot segment must also reject not just dot within longer path
targetArtifactRef .. (bare dot-dot as entire path) rejected R1-3; WHY: parent traversal at root level
targetArtifactRef foo/bar/ (trailing slash creating empty final segment) rejected R1-3; WHY: trailing slash leaves an empty segment

items.title: Implement minimum-specificity rule 3 so a class matcher can never be the sole present-in-red evidence
items.context: Section 1.3 rule 3: class matchers are supplementary for RED. An envelope whose only present-in-red matcher is a class matcher is rejected — otherwise a lone stderr-nonempty matcher would accept any failing run whatsoever. Class matchers remain exempt from rule 2.

items.title: Implement the exact section 1.11.4 entropy formula as byteLength times empirical per-byte Shannon entropy, total bits not per-symbol
items.context: entropyBits(value) = len(value) x H where len is BYTE length and H is the empirical per-byte Shannon entropy over the byte frequency distribution of value. TOTAL bits, not per-symbol. A per-symbol implementation yields provably different admissibility verdicts on a fixture table — that difference is the RED signal.

happy.desc: entropyBits for value Error: Cannot find module computed as byteLength(26) * H matches expected value within floating-point tolerance; WHY: confirms total-bits formula on a realistic error string

verification.selector: "Error: Cannot find module '/repo/dist/x.js'"  total= 185.06 perSymbol= 4.30 spec=ADMIT  rival=REJECT

edge.desc: DIFFERENTIAL: entropyBits(ab) = 2 * 1.0 = 2.0 total bits while per-symbol H = 1.0; entropyBits(aabb) = 4 * 1.0 = 4.0 total bits while per-symbol H = 1.0 -- total bits grows with length while per-symbol stays constant; WHY: proves the formula multiplies by byte length

verification.selector: formula anchors: ab=2.0 aabb=4.0 a=0.0 abcdefgh=24.0 (per-symbol rival is constant 1.0 for ab/aabb)

edge.desc: Single-byte value a yields entropyBits = 1 * 0 = 0 (one distinct byte, H=0); WHY: degenerate single-byte edge case where both formulas agree at zero

Multi-byte UTF-8 char (e.g. 4-byte emoji) yields byte length used for both len and frequency distribution; string.length differs from Buffer.byteLength; WHY: formula operates on raw bytes not code points or code units

adversarial.desc: FIXTURE TABLE: 8+ values where total-bits and per-symbol produce different admissibility verdicts under default policy (minMatcherEntropyBits=24) -- each row documents both formula results and asserts the total-bits verdict; WHY: this table IS the un-gameable proof that the correct formula is implemented, not the per-symbol variant

Value of 28 repeated identical bytes yields entropyBits=0 despite length >> 8, rejected by rule 2; per-symbol also gives 0 so this is NOT a differential case -- included to assert the formula handles the zero-entropy boundary where H=0

verification.selector: AGREE: 28 identical bytes, H = 0 so total = 0 (zero-entropy boundary)

NOTE: the value is 43 bytes, not the 26-byte string named in the intent text.

items.title: Compute assertionDigest as CANON over the assertion subobject including policyDigest and excluding assertionDigest
items.context: assertionDigest = W2a CANON over the assertion subobject with policyDigest INCLUDED and assertionDigest itself EXCLUDED. A validator that forgets to strip the field, or omits policyDigest, produces a different digest on the same envelope; both directions are asserted.

happy.desc: assertionDigest = canonDigestOmitting(assertion, assertionDigest) with policyDigest included recomputed over a fixture envelope matches the stored assertionDigest; WHY: confirms canonical digest scope is correct

edge.desc: NEGATIVE DIRECTION: canonDigest of the FULL assertion object (including assertionDigest field itself) produces a result that DIFFERS from the stored assertionDigest; WHY: a validator that forgets to strip assertionDigest gets a different digest -- both directions must be asserted

NEGATIVE DIRECTION: canonDigestOmitting with policyDigest removed from the assertion subobject produces a result that DIFFERS from the stored assertionDigest; WHY: a validator that omits policyDigest from the canonical subobject produces a different digest

adversarial.desc: Two assertions with identical matchers and proof but DIFFERENT policyDigest values yield DIFFERENT assertionDigest values; WHY: policyDigest is covered by assertionDigest so changing policy changes the assertion identity
Assertion roundtripped through JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)) produces the same assertionDigest; WHY: CANON is deterministic across serialization cycles, no key-order sensitivity

verificationEvidence.note: assert.equal(canonDigestOmitting(stored, "assertionDigest"), DIGEST) plus computeAssertionDigest(stored) === DIGEST: recomputing over the stored envelope with only the self field stripped — policyDigest still inside — reproduces the stored assertionDigest, which is also asserted to match /^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$/.

items.title: Validate the assertion against the committed target binding and recompute targetBindingDigest, returning tagged R1-1, R1-2, R1-3 and R1-6 rejections
items.context: Section 1.1.3: the assertion's adapterId and testCaseRef MUST equal the committed binding for its acceptanceTargetRef (read via the W2b committed-tree reader), and targetBindingDigest MUST recompute over the createdAt-stripped three-field subobject. Rejections carry the section 1.6 tags, mapped correctly: R1-1 = missing target-exercised proof; R1-2 = below-threshold or class-only matcher set (the minimum-specificity failure); R1-3 = matcher and path BOUNDS (a schema-bounds tag that explicitly covers path validation, NOT a specificity tag); R1-6 = unregistered or mismatched target binding. An implementer must not collapse R1-2 and R1-3 into one 'specificity' bucket.

happy.desc: Assertion with adapterId and testCaseRef matching committed binding and correct targetBindingDigest (recomputed over createdAt-stripped 3-field subobject) produces no rejection; WHY: full binding validation success path

verification.selector: baseline: one admissible present-in-red literal-line matcher

happy.desc: targetBindingDigest recomputed via canonDigest({acceptanceTargetRef, adapterId, testCaseRef}) matches stored digest; WHY: confirms createdAt stripping is ALLOWLIST-based (only three identity fields survive)

verification.selector: CHK-011: targetBindingDigest computed WITH createdAt included

edge.desc: Missing targetExercisedProof entirely produces rejection tagged R1-1 not R1-6; WHY: R1-1 is for missing target-exercised proof, distinct from binding mismatch

verification.selector: CHK-011: targetExercisedProof absent entirely is R1-1, NOT R1-6

edge.desc: Below-threshold literal (fails rule 2) produces rejection tagged R1-2 not R1-3; WHY: R1-2 is specificity failure, R1-3 is bounds -- they must not be collapsed

verification.selector: CHK-011: below-threshold literal is R1-2, NOT R1-3

edge.desc: Class-only present-in-red set produces rejection tagged R1-2 not R1-3; WHY: rule 3 failure is a minimum-specificity failure, correctly tagged R1-2

verification.selector: CHK-011: class-only present-in-red set is R1-2, NOT R1-3

edge.desc: Invalid targetArtifactRef path (absolute) produces rejection tagged R1-3 not R1-2; WHY: path validation is a schema-bounds failure explicitly under R1-3
Duplicate matcher id produces rejection tagged R1-3; WHY: schema-bounds violation
adapterId mismatching committed binding produces rejection tagged R1-6; WHY: unregistered or mismatched target binding

verification.selector: CHK-011: adapterId mismatching the committed binding

edge.desc: targetBindingDigest that would include createdAt in the canonical subobject fails recomputation producing R1-6; WHY: digest scope must strip createdAt and any storage metadata

verification.selector: CHK-011: targetBindingDigest computed WITH createdAt included

adversarial.desc: Correct adapterId but wrong testCaseRef produces rejection tagged R1-6 not R1-1; WHY: the binding EXISTS but the test case ref does not match -- this is a mismatch not a missing proof

verification.selector: CHK-011: correct adapterId but WRONG testCaseRef is R1-6 (mismatch), NOT R1-1 (missing)

adversarial.desc: Envelope triggering both R1-2 (below-threshold specificity) and R1-3 (invalid path) simultaneously reports both tags and neither suppresses the other; WHY: multiple rejection tags can co-occur on the same envelope

verification.selector: CHK-011: R1-2 and R1-3 co-occur and neither suppresses the other

verificationEvidence.note: The baseline envelope carries targetExercisedProof { method: harness-token, testCaseRef: npm-script:test:x, adapterId: npm-script@1, targetBindingDigest: targetBindingDigest(BINDING) } and is validated against COMMITTED (the same three fields plus createdAt); accept() asserts ok === true and a computed sha256 assertionDigest — the full binding-validation success path.

items.title: Land the read-only red_evidence_envelope_check command following the acceptance_topology_check house pattern and record the section 5.5 fence reasoning
items.context: red_evidence_envelope_check(storyId, assertionFile) validates a candidate envelope against the resolved policy and the story's registered binding BEFORE a run is spent, following the verified read-only house pattern of acceptance_topology_check, topology_critic_receipt_check and proofstory_gate_check in packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts (anchored by command name because that file drifts). It changes no gate verdict. SUCCESS OUTPUT CONTRACT: on an admissible envelope it reports the computed assertionDigest, the matched binding reference (acceptanceTargetRef, adapterId, testCaseRef) and the resolved policyDigest, so the operator can proceed; the smoke asserts that success transcript, not only the rejection cases. The story records explicitly that a read-only operator pre-flight is not a new query surface added to satisfy an enforcement need and therefore sits outside the section 5.5 fence.

verificationEvidence.note: Re-executed after review F-002/F-012/F-013 (three lanes converged) showed this harness claimed more than its mechanism could detect: a before/after SHA-256 snapshot of .lattice/ cannot observe a child process, yet the claim it carried covered process spawning. Two changes. First, the snapshot's claim is narrowed to exactly what it shows -- no file under .lattice/ created, modified or removed -- and the static registration facts are labelled declarations about wiring rather than behavioural evidence. items.title: Enforce the matcher array count bound of one to maxMatchers, rejecting a vacuous or oversized matcher set as R1-3
items.context: Spec section 1.1 point 1: matchers is an array of 1..policy.maxMatchers matcher objects. Section 1.6 R1-3 enumerates BOTH triggers explicitly: a record with 0 matchers, or more than policy.maxMatchers, is REJECTED. This is a COUNT bound and is distinct from the per-value byte-length bound maxMatcherLen already covered by CHK-002. A vacuous envelope carrying zero matchers is a gaming vector: it would assert nothing at all.

happy.desc: An envelope carrying a matcher count within 1..policy.maxMatchers under the frozen default policy is accepted by the count check.

verification.selector: CHK-015: exactly 1 matcher (inclusive lower count bound)

edge.desc: Exactly 1 matcher and exactly policy.maxMatchers matchers are both admissible (inclusive bounds on each end).

adversarial.desc: Committed test: an envelope with ZERO matchers is rejected with tag R1-3 and nothing else is reported as the primary failure — a vacuous envelope asserts nothing and must never be admissible.
Committed test: an envelope with policy.maxMatchers + 1 matchers is rejected with tag R1-3.

items.title: Require a class matcher value to name a registered matcherClassRegistry entry case-sensitively, rejecting an unregistered class as R1-3
items.context: Spec section 1.1 point 1: for kind=class the value MUST be the exact, case-sensitive name key of a policy.matcherClassRegistry entry (section 1.2); a value naming no registry entry is rejected. Section 1.6 R1-3 lists 'a class value naming no registry entry' among its triggers. This is a registry-escape gaming vector: an unregistered class name would otherwise pass through unchecked. Distinct from CHK-008, which governs whether a class matcher may be the SOLE present-in-red evidence.

happy.desc: A class matcher whose value exactly matches a registered matcherClassRegistry name under the frozen default policy is accepted by the membership check.

verification.selector: CHK-016: class value exactly naming a registered matcherClassRegistry entry

edge.desc: Membership is CASE-SENSITIVE: a value differing only in case from a registered name is rejected.

verification.selector: CHK-016: class value "Stderr-Nonempty" names no registry entry

edge.desc: The registry consulted is the one resolved from policy, so a policy with a different registry changes the admissible class set.

verification.selector: CHK-016: a class registered ONLY in the default policy is unregistered under a custom registry

adversarial.desc: Committed test: a class matcher naming no registry entry at all is rejected with tag R1-3 — the registry-escape vector is closed.

adversarial.desc: Committed test: the rejection is tagged R1-3 (matcher and path bounds), NOT R1-2 — an unregistered class name is a bounds failure, not a minimum-specificity failure.

auditLog.addedTitle: Enforce the matcher array count bound of one to maxMatchers, rejecting a vacuous or oversized matcher set as R1-3
auditLog.addedContext: Spec section 1.1 point 1: matchers is an array of 1..policy.maxMatchers matcher objects. Section 1.6 R1-3 enumerates BOTH triggers explicitly: a record with 0 matchers, or more than policy.maxMatchers, is REJECTED. This is a COUNT bound and is distinct from the per-value byte-length bound maxMatcherLen already covered by CHK-002. A vacuous envelope carrying zero matchers is a gaming vector: it would assert nothing at all.

auditLog.reason: PLAN scope reviewer (scope-check _hash b67028b4) found the section 1.6 R1-3 class-registry membership check named in no checklist title; CHK-008 covers only the sole-present-in-red rule, not membership. Adding as a named item so gate review covers it.
auditLog.addedTitle: Require a class matcher value to name a registered matcherClassRegistry entry case-sensitively, rejecting an unregistered class as R1-3
auditLog.addedContext: Spec section 1.1 point 1: for kind=class the value MUST be the exact, case-sensitive name key of a policy.matcherClassRegistry entry (section 1.2); a value naming no registry entry is rejected. Section 1.6 R1-3 lists 'a class value naming no registry entry' among its triggers. This is a registry-escape gaming vector: an unregistered class name would otherwise pass through unchecked. Distinct from CHK-008, which governs whether a class matcher may be the SOLE present-in-red evidence.
